newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish stocks dive on government concerns.
newsitem.headline: Turkish stocks dive on government concerns.

text.p: Istanbul stocks fell sharply in early trading on Thursday over concerns about the fate of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's coalition government, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 was down 6.79 pct at 1,428 in the morning session. Turkish financial and capital markets reopened on Thursday after a 6-1/2 day holiday for the Moslem Eid al-Adha festival and Children's Day.
"The market turned cautious beacuse of increased political concerns. The stock exchange index may fall further today and tomorrow," said Mustafa Acar, general manager of Ari Securities.
Press reports that the main oppostion leader Mesut Yilmaz had prepared alternative government models to replace the existing coalition dominated the morning session, brokers said.
Yilmaz, chairman of Motherland Party, offered two different government combinations, grouping several different parties.
Existing party leaders, seen by many as the stumbling block to past deals, would be excluded from his formulas to take the country to elections in 1998 or 1999, daily Hurriyet reported.
Serdar Surer from Ekinciler Securities said political worries, accompanied by a liquidity shortage, were likely to grip the market.
The market is short of 71.7 trillion lira ($534 million) on Thursday according to the central bank figures.

An upcoming meeting of Turkey's National Security Council on April 26 has also aggravated political concerns. The military members of the council are expected to increase pressure on the reluctant government to implement anti-Islamist measures.
